The Ebola outbreak is the deadliest of Congo’s 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016

Six months after an Ebola outbreak was declared in Congo, the disease remains out of control and efforts to contain it are faltering.

More than 11,000 cases have been recorded, and nearly half of those infected have died, according to Government data. It is the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.

Basic containment measures, including contact tracing and isolation, remain inadequate, raising doubts about authorities' ability to halt the outbreak. Experts say there is little chance of bringing it under control within the next year.

By the time the outbreak was announced in mid-May, 43 deaths had already been recorded, suggesting the virus had circulated undetected for an extended period. It has since spread to eight of the country's 26 provinces, moving at a pace aid groups have likened to wildfire.

New hotspots continue to emerge, stretching an already strained health care system.

Community transmission remains high. According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, 80% of new cases are being detected outside health surveillance, meaning most infections have not been tracked by authorities.

fullParagraphs: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also warned the Kremlin was “betting everything” on this winter’s military campaign
Mr. Zelenskyy also warned the Kremlin was “betting everything” on this winter’s military campaign.
Moscow has pounded Ukraine in the run-up to the colder months, with Russian President Vladimir Putin showing no sign of backing down.
U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met both Mr. Putin and Mr. Zelenskyy separately on Thursday after two days of talks with their delegations in Abu Dhabi, which ended with no breakthrough.
“The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Mr. Zelenskyy said.
“After providing Ukraine with this kind of defence support, seeing this kind of development of our army and this strength in our defence, they cannot simply let Ukraine go,” he added.
He said the discussion showed that “NATO is back on the agenda” for Ukraine.
Ukraine has long sought to enter the military alliance, which Moscow has considered a red line.
NATO and Washington have not yet commented directly on Mr. Zelenskyy’s account.
Mr. Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, later posted on X that media had reported “maximalist propositions proposed by both sides, along with strong political rhetoric”.

“However, we are determined to continue the hard work, maintain the confidentiality necessary for sensitive negotiations, and find a pathway to end this horrible war,” he said, adding “several new ideas emerged from the discussions and are now being explored.”

articles.title: What is ‘food is medicine’? – 2 experts explain this decades-old approach to healthcare that is taking on new life
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Access to healthy food would be considered as essential as medications for patients with chronic illness

Mountains of scientific evidence support both the negative and positive effects of our eating habits on our health . Research shows that a healthy diet can help those suffering from chronic health conditions like Type 2 diabetes , heart disease and high blood pressure .

This is where “food is medicine” comes in. Food is medicine, also known as “food as medicine” and “food prescriptions,” is a movement dedicated to providing healthy food – fruits, vegetables and sometimes healthy proteins – based on a clinician’s prescription in order to prevent, manage or treat specific clinical conditions .
Prescribing food to patients is intended to convey that food is just as important as medication for health and wellness.

As researchers whose work focuses on food access and health in rural communities, we have firsthand experience running food is medicine programs in our local area in northern Mississippi. This experience has shown us the benefits and limitations of these programs in our community.

Food is medicine programs can be delivered through curated food boxes, grocery vouchers and medically tailored meals. Most programs are collaborations between nonprofit organizations, health clinics and healthcare providers. The goal of food is medicine is to improve patient health, especially for those with chronic conditions, while reducing healthcare costs.

Increasingly, food is medicine programs have become lifelines for people with food insecurity. In 2024, more than 47 million Americans, including 7.3 million children, lived in food-insecure households – meaning they were at some point uncertain of having, or did not have, enough food for everyone in the household.

Internationally, the number of people experiencing hunger rises to roughly 673 million . Rural populations are more likely to be food insecure due to the loss of local grocery stores and distance from urban centers. Unlike a food bank, food is medicine programs provide only healthy foods, which are often curated by a dietitian, to optimize patient health.

Though food is medicine isn’t formally connected to the Make American Healthy Again movement , U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. has brought new energy and attention to the concept. In January 2026, the second Trump administration launched a campaign encouraging Americans to “ Eat Real Food .”

But the food is medicine movement actually began more than 60 years ago. One of the early providers who prescribed food as medicine was civil rights activist and multiple Nobel Peace Prize winner Dr. Jack Geiger . In the 1960s, he co-founded community health centers in South Boston and the Mississippi Delta.
When government officials chastised him for prescribing food to patients in the Delta, Geiger responded, “The last time I looked at my textbooks, the most specific therapy for malnutrition was food.”

articles.title: 91% of studies in India in last 5 decades linked air pollution to health effects: Analysis
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16

An analysis of more than 180 epidemiological studies examining the health impacts of air pollution across India has found that over 91% of them reported at least one adverse health association with air pollution exposure.

These studies, published between 1975 and 2025, also noted that health impacts extend beyond respiratory diseases to cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, pregnancy complications, impaired child growth, tumours, blood disorders, mental and neurocognitive disorders, among others.

The analysis, released on Friday, was done by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation focused on revealing the trends, causes, and health impacts, as well as the solutions, to air pollution.

Notably, out of 180 studies, only 40 examined air pollution's impact on rural populations, of which 38 reported at least one adverse health association, indicating that air pollution's health impacts are not confined to urban areas.

Further, most studies were conducted on Delhi (26) to examine the link between health and air pollution. The national capital was followed by Punjab with 13 studies, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with 11 each, West Bengal with 10, Tamil Nadu with nine, Karnataka with eight and Telangana with seven, the report said.

In a statement, CREA analyst Manoj Kumar said, "The findings highlight the need to move beyond a city-centric approach and explicitly include rural areas through a regional, airshed-based approach in the next phase of National Clean Air Programme (NCAP 2.0)."
Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16.

Among studies examining gaseous pollutants, statistically significant adverse health associations were reported for increased mortality, acute respiratory hospital and emergency visits, asthma-related hospital admissions, and impaired lung function.

Beyond their direct health effects, gaseous pollutants such as SOx and NOx also contribute to secondary PM2.5 formation by undergoing atmospheric chemical reactions to form sulphate and nitrate particles, respectively.

Kumar said, "Air pollution mitigation must adopt a multipollutant approach, addressing gaseous precursors that contribute to secondary PM2.5 and ground-level ozone formation. This requires emission reductions at major sources, including industries, power plants, residential cooking, and other combustion activities."

articles.title: COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns

Exposure to extreme heat during pregnancy can lead to severe outcomes, including preterm birth, stillbirth and congenital abnormalities in newborns, prompting experts at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to highlight maternal health risks and call for targeted adaptation strategies.

The issue comes into focus as countries at COP31 prepare to discuss progress towards the Global Goal on Adaptation, a framework to help nations develop key adaptation measures, including those needed to address the health impacts of climate change.
However, translating growing recognition of climate-related health risks into action remains a challenge, particularly in the absence of adequate financial support.
According to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), only about one per cent of formal climate finance under its financial mechanism is currently directed towards health.
The broader issue of adaptation finance for developing nations is also expected to feature prominently in discussions in the coming days.

Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of COP31, Alan Dangour, Director of Climate and Health at the Wellcome Trust, said the foundation is seeking to highlight the evidence of heat-related impacts on pregnant women through three key areas -- elevating the issues as a risk for women, developing guidelines and preparing health systems.

“We have three key points: recognising that pregnant women are a particularly vulnerable group when it comes to climate-driven extreme heat, developing guidelines to help nurses, midwives and doctors respond to the challenges pregnant women face during heatwaves, and prepare health systems for a new world shaped by climate change, and identify the most vulnerable people so they are protected,” Dangour said.
He said pregnant women were not always recognised as a particularly vulnerable group and stressed that health systems must specifically account for their needs and risks during heatwaves.

“At the moment they are not recognised as such, and they need to be included in clinical guidelines. When it comes to data, we are keen that countries record the impacts of climate change on pregnant women and then work out how their guidelines and processes can protect them,” he said.
“That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said.

📰 COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns

Exposure to extreme heat during pregnancy can lead to severe outcomes, including preterm birth, stillbirth and congenital abnormalities in newborns, prompting experts at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to highlight maternal health risks and call for targeted adaptation strategies.

The issue comes into focus as countries at COP31 prepare to discuss progress towards the Global Goal on Adaptation, a framework to help nations develop key adaptation measures, including those needed to address the health impacts of climate change.

However, translating growing recognition of climate-related health risks into action remains a challenge, particularly in the absence of adequate financial support.

According to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), only about one per cent of formal climate finance under its financial mechanism is currently directed towards health.

The broader issue of adaptation finance for developing nations is also expected to feature prominently in discussions in the coming days.

Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of COP31, Alan Dangour, Director of Climate and Health at the Wellcome Trust, said the foundation is seeking to highlight the evidence of heat-related impacts on pregnant women through three key areas -- elevating the issues as a risk for women, developing guidelines and preparing health systems.

“We have three key points: recognising that pregnant women are a particularly vulnerable group when it comes to climate-driven extreme heat, developing guidelines to help nurses, midwives and doctors respond to the challenges pregnant women face during heatwaves, and prepare health systems for a new world shaped by climate change, and identify the most vulnerable people so they are protected,” Dangour said.

He said pregnant women were not always recognised as a particularly vulnerable group and stressed that health systems must specifically account for their needs and risks during heatwaves.

“At the moment they are not recognised as such, and they need to be included in clinical guidelines. When it comes to data, we are keen that countries record the impacts of climate change on pregnant women and then work out how their guidelines and processes can protect them,” he said.

“That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said.

The 59th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu, marking World Diabetes Day, explores the everyday realities of living with diabetes and approaches to managing the condition over time.

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 closes in on a light-day in interstellar space for new distance record
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: NASA is looking at another 18,000 years before the spacecraft achieves a full light-year and more than double that before it comes near another star
NASA's Voyager 1 is about to become humanity's first object to reach one light-day from Earth as it pushes ever deeper into interstellar space.
That's a mind-blowing distance of more than 26 billion kilometres for the spacecraft launched 49 years ago.

When Voyager 1 reaches that remarkable milestone on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), its radio signals will take precisely 24 hours travelling at the speed of light to reach Earth — in other words, one light-day.
NASA is looking at another 18,000 years before the spacecraft achieves a full light-year and more than double that before it comes near another star.
Project manager Suzanne Dodd sees Voyager 1 as Earth's ambassador hurtling between stars while providing a “sense of wonder” on the home front.
“It's a national treasure,” she told The Associated Press . “Really extraordinary.”

To celebrate this moment, NASA is urging people from all corners to grab their phone or a flashlight to create a wave of golden light after sunset on Tuesday (November 17), using Morse code to spell the letters V-G-R, Voyager's call sign, into the night sky.

Despite sporadic problems typical of old age, Voyager 1 and its twin Voyager 2 continue to send back science and engineering data as they zoom toward different points in space at 61,000 kph. Although launched two weeks before its sibling in 1977, Voyager 2 won't reach the one light-day mark until 2035.

Voyager 1 swept past Jupiter and Saturn to scientists' delight in 1979 and 1980, respectively, before exiting the solar system. It reached what NASA defines as interstellar space — the expansive region between star systems — in 2012. Voyager 2 visited those two planets plus Uranus and Neptune, also sending back stunning photos, before entering interstellar space in 2018.

Almost every day, the Voyagers beam back details about their never-before-explored environment: the strength and direction of the magnetic field as well as tidbits about the surrounding pressure, dust and galactic cosmic rays. They're a bit like weather satellites, according to Dodd, who's worked with the Voyagers since 1984.

articles.title: In latest ‘encounter’, West Bengal police kill a man accused of shooting at a constable two days ago
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is the fifth instance of an accused killed in police firing in West Bengal, within six months of the BJP coming to power in the State; this was an “extrajudicial execution”, says civil society group

A man accused of opening fire at a police constable at Santiniketan in West Bengal 's Birbhum district on Friday (November 13, 2026) was killed in a gunfight with the law enforcers on Sunday (November 15, 2026), a senior officer said.
Ratan Sheikh was killed after he opened fire at a police team while trying to evade arrest at a brick kiln in Nanoor in the same district.
This was the fifth police encounter in West Bengal in six months since the BJP came to power in the State.

Sheikh, a history-sheeter who was absconding, allegedly shot at constable Biswajit Das, injuring him in the leg, during an arrest attempt at Laik Bazar in Santiniketan police station area on November 13.
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, while reacting to the development, asks reporters, "If someone opens fire at the police, should the police offer them sweets"

articles.title: India, Bangladesh leaderships should support temporary renewal of Ganga Water Treaty, says expert
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Full revision of the Ganga Water Treaty is not possible in the four weeks left before it expires, says Manjur Ahmed Chowdhury, former Chairman of the National River Conservation Commission of Bangladesh, but ‘having a bad treaty is better than not having any treaty at all’

There is no possibility of a fully revised India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Treaty in the mere four weeks left before the 30-year-old treaty expires, Manjur Ahmed Chowdhury, former Chairman of the National River Conservation Commission of Bangladesh said on Sunday (November 15, 2026). The current treaty could be renewed for three to five years “at the last moment”, Mr. Chowdhury said, but clearance would be needed at the highest level of political leadership for it.

“Four weeks is not sufficient for revising the old Ganga Water Treaty as river water treaties require more time to finalise. But having a bad treaty is also better than not having any treaty at all. We can at least opt for a renewal of the treaty for three to five years, if the political leaderships of both sides give the green signal,” Mr. Chowdhury said.

He cautioned Bangladesh on the upcoming agriculture season of February when, as in every year, Bangladesh’s dependence on Ganga water will increase. “Without a treaty, India will not have any commitment to release water at regular intervals and that might pose a major problem for Bangladesh’s agriculture sector, economy as well as ecology,” Mr. Chowdhury said.

The Ganga Water Treaty was signed in December 1996 by Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda of India and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina of Bangladesh. Prior to the signing of the treaty, for eight years between 1988 and 1996, Bangladesh suffered due to unpredictability in the supply of the Ganga’s water, and the treaty had ensured predictability, which helped Bangladesh, Mr. Chowdhury said.

The treaty stated that “sharing between India and Bangladesh of the Ganga waters at Farakka by ten days periods from the 1st January to the 31st May every year will be with reference to the formula at Annexure 1 of the treaty”. The Annexure 1 of the treaty had ensured that if the Farakka barrage would have 70,000 cusecs or less water, then the share of water would be 50% for both India and Bangladesh. The Annexure 1 also gave out similar division of water in Farakka for 70,000 to 75,000 cusecs, and for storage beyond 75,000 cusecs.

It would be difficult for Bangladesh to demand its share of waters of the Ganga without a legally and diplomatically binding treaty, Mr. Chowdhury said. “During the Ershad (President of Bangladesh from 1983 to 1990) years, we suffered from this lack of predictability, and reverting to that era will be a setback,” he said, adding that the Government of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had not managed Bangladesh’s foreign policy requirements effectively as river water supply was related to Dhaka’s foreign policy.

“The foreign policy of the government has become unhinged from real requirements. At the moment, there is an urgent need for agreement between the political leaderships of Bangladesh and India to ensure the Ganga Water Treaty remains on track,” Mr. Chowdhury said.

The Ganga Water Treaty should have been revised and updated taking into account the problems, including sedimentation and the changes that the river had experienced over the last three decades, Mr. Chowdhury said in his conversation with The Hindu . “These updates could not be done in the last few months because of lack of meetings, and the Joint River Commission has turned out to be quite weak in performing its duties,” he said adding, “I am still hopeful that, at least by the first week of December, the two sides will act to save the treaty. But that would have to be a dramatic development.”

articles.title: Telangana government urged to clear fee reimbursement dues of pharmacy colleges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana Pharmacy Colleges Managements Association, comprising 120 private colleges and 3 government colleges, with approximately 70,000 students, has urged the government to clear the fee reimbursement dues that are meagre compared to others.

The newly elected president Pulla Ramesh Babu and general secretary Kadiyala Satish said the government’s annual fee reimbursement liability towards pharmacy institutions is only around Rs 120 to Rs 130 crore, covering approximately 70,000 students across Telangana. They requested the government to clear the final year students’ dues first.

They said pharmacy students in Telangana were being absorbed in jobs immediately due to its pharma industry here contributing nearly 50–60% of the country’s pharmaceutical production. There is also a huge scope for research and employment in the clinical sector.

Regarding fees, they said Telangana has among the lowest pharmacy education fees in the country, at ₹50,000–₹60,000 annually, compared to approximately ₹1 lakh in other states. Nearly 90% of colleges operate solely on tuition fees.

Other newly elected office bearers include A. Prabhakar Reddy, Ashok Reddy, Habeebuddin, Talla Varun, Madhusdhan Reddy, Chiranjeevi and Naveen. K. Ramdass and T. Jayapal Reddy will be the chief advisor and honorary president, respectively.

articles.title: Czechs gather in big numbers to reject government's plan to overhaul funding of public media
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The massive protest took place at the capital's Letná Park, where huge crowds gathered during the 1989 Velvet Revolution, which ended more than 40 years of communist rule in the country

Hundreds of thousands of people rallied in Prague on Sunday (November 15, 2026) against a plan by the government of Czech billionaire Andrej Babis to overhaul funding for public broadcasters that many say will erode media independence and democracy.
The massive protest took place at the capital's Letná Park, where huge crowds gathered during the 1989 Velvet Revolution, which ended more than 40 years of communist rule in the country.

The rally, just two days before the anniversary of the 1989 protests, drew an estimated 350,000 people, said Mikulas Minar, the lead organizer from the Million Moments for Democracy group. They demanded that the government withdraw its plan and expressed concern that Babis and his coalition partners pose a threat to democracy.
“We do witness here something extraordinary today,” Mr. Minar said.

Under the plan, the country's public radio and television broadcasters would be financed from the state budget, replacing the existing system of regular fees paid by individuals, households and businesses. The broadcasters would receive about 15% less money than they do now, which could lead to layoffs, limited production and program cancellations.

Critics say the overhaul would give the three-party coalition the means to take control of the media, similar to what populist governments did in Slovakia under Prime Minister Robert Fico and in Hungary, before former Prime Minister Viktor Orban was ousted from power in April.
“We refuse the Slovak scenario,” one protest banner read. “Hands off the media,” said another.

The ruling coalition unexpectedly moved ahead with the plan in the lower house of Parliament on Oct. 24. Its lawmakers limited the opposition's speaking time before voting at 4.36 a.m. to advance the bill through the first of three parliamentary readings.

Thousands took to the streets the following day to protest the rushed process, and public media employees went on strike on Nov. 3. The strike was backed by labor unions, universities, students, churches, artists, athletes and international media organizations, among others.
“We are here to stand up against the rule by force in the style of 4:36,” Mr. Minár said Sunday (November 15, 2026), referring to the time the bill cleared its first reading.

articles.title: Lalit Modi announces he has acquired British citizenship; ‘proudly’ calls it home
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Lalit Modi announced on X that he had been naturalised as a British citizen on September 20; says United Kingdom has been my home for many years

Indian Premier League (IPL) founder Lalit Modi, who has had a number of cases and investigations against him in India, announced over the weekend that he had become a British citizen. The loss of Indian citizenship – which is automatic when one accepts the citizenship of another country – further complicates the process of extraditing Mr. Modi to India.
Mr. Modi announced on X that he had been naturalised as a British citizen on September 20.

New Delhi has repeatedly pressed the U.K. for the return of Mr. Modi, along with others such as diamond jeweller Nirav Modi and entrepreneur Vija Mallya, to India to face legal proceedings. Prime Minister Narendra Modi made requests to his (then) British counterpart Keir Starmer for the return of “economic offenders and fugitives” in July 2025, when he visited the U.K., according to a government readout of their meeting.
Mr. Lalit Modi announced his new citizenship status in person at the Oxford Union on Saturday (November 14, 2026), he said, noting that November 14 was also the birthday of King Charles III.
“Thank you to my family, friends and everyone who has been part of this journey, and to the Oxford Union for providing such a memorable occasion to share this news,” he said.
“The United Kingdom has been my home for many years,” he said.

He was accused in India of financial irregularities and money laundering, as well as violating the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), stemming from his time as the Vice President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) during the 2009-2010 period. A case against Mr. Lalit Modi under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, based on an FIR filed by the Tamil Nadu police on October 13, 2010.
A non-bailable warrant was issued against Mr. Lalit Modi in 2015 after he failed to respond to multiple summonses from the Enforcement Directorate (ED).

🇬🇧 A PROUD MOMENT. A NEW CHAPTER. Today, 14 November 2026, I had the honour of addressing the Oxford Union, where I publicly shared a very special and personal milestone. I AM PROUD TO BE A BRITISH CITIZEN. 🇬🇧 On 15 September 2026, surrounded by family and friends, I celebrated my British citizenship at a ceremony that will always hold a special place in my heart. The United Kingdom has been my home for many years. It is a country I have come to admire and appreciate deeply — its people, institutions, traditions and values. Becoming British is a privilege and a responsibility that I embrace with pride, gratitude and a genuine sense of belonging. My life's journey has been shaped by different cultures and experiences, and I look forward to continuing to contribute positively to the country I proudly call home. Thank you to my family, friends and everyone who has been part of this journey, and to the Oxford Union for providing such a memorable occasion to share this news. A new chapter, with much to look forward to. And on His Majesty King Charles III's birthday, a particularly special day to share this moment. God Save the King! 🇬🇧👑 Lalit Modi Founder IPL #BritishCitizen #OxfordUnion #UnitedKingdom #GodSaveTheKing

🌐 International & Geopolitics 📅 15 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 5 Min Read

📰 Lalit Modi announces he has acquired British citizenship; ‘proudly’ calls it home

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Lalit Modi announced on X that he had been naturalised as a British citizen on September 20; says United Kingdom has been my home for many years

Indian Premier League (IPL) founder Lalit Modi, who has had a number of cases and investigations against him in India, announced over the weekend that he had become a British citizen. The loss of Indian citizenship – which is automatic when one accepts the citizenship of another country – further complicates the process of extraditing Mr. Modi to India.

Mr. Modi announced on X that he had been naturalised as a British citizen on September 20.

New Delhi has repeatedly pressed the U.K. for the return of Mr. Modi, along with others such as diamond jeweller Nirav Modi and entrepreneur Vija Mallya, to India to face legal proceedings. Prime Minister Narendra Modi made requests to his (then) British counterpart Keir Starmer for the return of “economic offenders and fugitives” in July 2025, when he visited the U.K., according to a government readout of their meeting.

Mr. Lalit Modi announced his new citizenship status in person at the Oxford Union on Saturday (November 14, 2026), he said, noting that November 14 was also the birthday of King Charles III.

“Thank you to my family, friends and everyone who has been part of this journey, and to the Oxford Union for providing such a memorable occasion to share this news,” he said.

“The United Kingdom has been my home for many years,” he said.

He was accused in India of financial irregularities and money laundering, as well as violating the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), stemming from his time as the Vice President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) during the 2009-2010 period. A case against Mr. Lalit Modi under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, based on an FIR filed by the Tamil Nadu police on October 13, 2010.

A non-bailable warrant was issued against Mr. Lalit Modi in 2015 after he failed to respond to multiple summonses from the Enforcement Directorate (ED).

🇬🇧 A PROUD MOMENT. A NEW CHAPTER. Today, 14 November 2026, I had the honour of addressing the Oxford Union, where I publicly shared a very special and personal milestone. I AM PROUD TO BE A BRITISH CITIZEN. 🇬🇧 On 15 September 2026, surrounded by family and friends, I celebrated my British citizenship at a ceremony that will always hold a special place in my heart. The United Kingdom has been my home for many years. It is a country I have come to admire and appreciate deeply — its people, institutions, traditions and values. Becoming British is a privilege and a responsibility that I embrace with pride, gratitude and a genuine sense of belonging. My life's journey has been shaped by different cultures and experiences, and I look forward to continuing to contribute positively to the country I proudly call home. Thank you to my family, friends and everyone who has been part of this journey, and to the Oxford Union for providing such a memorable occasion to share this news. A new chapter, with much to look forward to. And on His Majesty King Charles III's birthday, a particularly special day to share this moment. God Save the King! 🇬🇧👑 Lalit Modi Founder IPL #BritishCitizen #OxfordUnion #UnitedKingdom #GodSaveTheKing

On February 6, 2017, the ED requested the U.K. authorities to transfer Mr. Lalit Modi to India to face justice in relation to the non-bailable warrant. It used the Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT) process for this.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Megaspeed International has come under the scanner after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm, is in the spotlight after the alleged extramarital affair of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with one of the company’s former executives, Alice Huang. Ms Huang is accused of being a Chinese spy.
On November 15, 2026, Megaspeed said that Alice Huang had officially left Megaspeed on August 30, 2025 and had no current role at the company.
“Megaspeed does not ​comment on ‌Ms. Huang’s personal and private matters,” the company added in ‌a statement.
“Megaspeed is ​aware of recent media reports ⁠containing assertions about our business, supply chain ‌and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence.”
The company said it conducted “legitimate ‌and lawful business” and ​had retained external legal counsel to ⁠conduct a thorough internal ⁠investigation.

According to its website , Megaspeed is an Nvidia cloud partner in the Asia-Pacific region and a core business partner of Nvidia’s computing power cloud business. It adds that “we provide privatized, customized computing power product services covering NVIDIA’s entire GPU product line.”

A Reuters report says that Megaspeed International was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International before changing its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023. It adds that the company is wholly owned by Singapore-registered Swiftdata, incorporated in October 2023, which says providing hosting services by non-data centers is its principal activity.

Reuters adds that Megaspeed’s assets increased sharply to $3 billion in 2024 from $33 million in 2023, its business filings showed. It reported an after-tax loss of $20 million ‌in ⁠2024, versus a loss of $21,283 a year earlier, while revenue jumped to $294 million from zero. Its cash flow statement showed $844,555 went to investing activities in 2024, after financing activities brought in cash of $10 million the previous year.

According to the company’s LinkedIn , it has around 2-10 employees and 23 associated members. The interactive map by LinkedIn shows that Megaspeed has offices in Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia; Senayan City, Indonesia; and is headquartered in the Central Region of Singapore.

Washington has restricted the export of Nvidia’s most cutting-edge silicon chips to China, citing national security concerns. The move is also seen as a measure to stay ahead in the field of artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Binance hack reveals crypto's uphill battle against hackers
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Cryptocurrency exchanges present unusually attractive targets because hackers can identify wallets holding enormous sums of readily transferable digital assets ⁠and, in some cases, the employees with access

An elite North Korean hacking group’s $6.3 billion theft from Binance is renewing scrutiny of a longstanding weakness in the cryptocurrency industry: hackers may need to ‌compromise only one employee to get inside, while inconsistent security practices can allow them to turn that foothold ​into a massive theft.

The October 29 heist, described by experts as the largest cryptocurrency theft ever, unfolded in ⁠a matter of minutes after months of planning and preparation, according to Binance’s initial investigation.

Cybersecurity experts said the attack raises questions not only about how exchanges defend employees against sophisticated social engineering, but also about whether they have adequate internal controls to limit what an attacker can do once an employee’s computer or ‌credentials are compromised.

Social engineering is a well-understood threat in the industry, said Jonathan Alexander, chief technology officer of S&P Global’s OpenZeppelin, a blockchain security provider. The bigger question, he said, is why exchanges do not have stronger internal safeguards ‌and circuit breakers to prevent an attacker who breaches an engineer’s computer — like what happened at Binance — from escalating access and ‌moving ⁠assets.

Varying cybersecurity practices across the industry compound the problem, Alexander said, along with a longstanding aversion among some cryptocurrency advocates ⁠to controls they view as inconsistent with blockchain’s decentralized ethos that sometimes views things such as limits on transaction amounts and automatic reviews of patterns of spending as infringing on inherent privacy rights.

“I think that falsely, that has led some people to think that things like circuit breakers, things like more controls on the accounts, would be ​unacceptable or would be absolutely in conflict with that ‌need to avoid censorship,” Alexander said. “In my view, you can have security controls and have protections against that.”

The Binance attack is the latest in a string of major cryptocurrency hacks that have resulted in more than $22.3 billion in stolen funds since 2021, according to blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis. The scale of the losses has intensified debate over whether exchanges need more consistent standards governing access, ‌transaction controls and other defenses.

“I do expect we’ll see more clarity and standardization in the kind of cybersecurity expectations and, hopefully, requirements ​for investor protection and trust,” Alexander said. “These things show why it has to change.”

Cryptocurrency exchanges present unusually attractive targets because hackers can identify wallets holding enormous sums of readily transferable digital assets ⁠and, in some cases, the employees with access to the systems controlling them.
That has made engineers and IT workers prime targets for elaborate social-engineering operations.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 15 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Binance hack reveals crypto's uphill battle against hackers

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action

Cryptocurrency exchanges present unusually attractive targets because hackers can identify wallets holding enormous sums of readily transferable digital assets ⁠and, in some cases, the employees with access

An elite North Korean hacking group’s $6.3 billion theft from Binance is renewing scrutiny of a longstanding weakness in the cryptocurrency industry: hackers may need to ‌compromise only one employee to get inside, while inconsistent security practices can allow them to turn that foothold ​into a massive theft.

The October 29 heist, described by experts as the largest cryptocurrency theft ever, unfolded in ⁠a matter of minutes after months of planning and preparation, according to Binance’s initial investigation.

Cybersecurity experts said the attack raises questions not only about how exchanges defend employees against sophisticated social engineering, but also about whether they have adequate internal controls to limit what an attacker can do once an employee’s computer or ‌credentials are compromised.

Social engineering is a well-understood threat in the industry, said Jonathan Alexander, chief technology officer of S&P Global’s OpenZeppelin, a blockchain security provider. The bigger question, he said, is why exchanges do not have stronger internal safeguards ‌and circuit breakers to prevent an attacker who breaches an engineer’s computer — like what happened at Binance — from escalating access and ‌moving ⁠assets.

Varying cybersecurity practices across the industry compound the problem, Alexander said, along with a longstanding aversion among some cryptocurrency advocates ⁠to controls they view as inconsistent with blockchain’s decentralized ethos that sometimes views things such as limits on transaction amounts and automatic reviews of patterns of spending as infringing on inherent privacy rights.

“I think that falsely, that has led some people to think that things like circuit breakers, things like more controls on the accounts, would be ​unacceptable or would be absolutely in conflict with that ‌need to avoid censorship,” Alexander said. “In my view, you can have security controls and have protections against that.”

The Binance attack is the latest in a string of major cryptocurrency hacks that have resulted in more than $22.3 billion in stolen funds since 2021, according to blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis. The scale of the losses has intensified debate over whether exchanges need more consistent standards governing access, ‌transaction controls and other defenses.

“I do expect we’ll see more clarity and standardization in the kind of cybersecurity expectations and, hopefully, requirements ​for investor protection and trust,” Alexander said. “These things show why it has to change.”

Cryptocurrency exchanges present unusually attractive targets because hackers can identify wallets holding enormous sums of readily transferable digital assets ⁠and, in some cases, the employees with access to the systems controlling them.

That has made engineers and IT workers prime targets for elaborate social-engineering operations.

Ai+ Smartphone on Friday announced to increase the price of its smartphone portfolio by up to ₹3,000 . The new prices will be effective November 11.
The smartphone prices are expected to rise up again by up to 10% post Diwali due to memory crisis, lesser inventories and rupee depreciation against US dollar.
“With fresh inventory being procured at higher memory and component costs, the company has advanced its planned price revision to reflect the updated cost structure,” the company said.

Ai+ Smartphone, a new homegrown smartphone brand, sold over ten lakh devices during the Q3, 2026. “The decision follows stronger-than-anticipated consumer demand, with sales exceeding initial projections and existing inventory being exhausted ahead of schedule,” it added.
Recently, another Indian smartphone brand, Lava, said to increase its smartphone prices by up to ₹3,000 post Diwali.
Overall, Indian smartphone shipments went down to a decade low by 20% during the third quarter due diminishing demand and rising average smartphone price (ASP) of the phones.

articles.title: Oppo Pad Mini Review | A refreshing take on what a tablet can be
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: At a time when most tablets are getting bigger, the Pad Mini takes a different route. It is compact, remarkably light and designed for people who want a tablet they can comfortably carry around

Oppo has launched the Pad Mini in India at ₹94,999. And that is quite a price to ask for a tablet in the Indian market. Rashmi Ramesh, 40, from Mumbai, has been managing Hashimoto’s thyroiditis for nearly two decades. And yet, she continues to experience hair fall and fluctuations in weight. Although she was diagnosed when she was 20, she says symptoms such as puffiness around her eyes and face, lethargy and weight gain had begun when she was about 10.

Staying fit and managing her health require constant attention to sleep, diet and exercise, she says. “It is tough to stay fit. I have to work much harder than someone who doesn’t live with Hashimoto’s.” During pregnancy, she experienced substantial weight gain and water retention, along with puffiness. Managing her condition requires constant vigilance.

articles.title: A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal

Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. articles.title: Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

articles.summary: The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP
articles.keyPoints:
• The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP
• As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.
• Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

fullParagraphs: ASEAN leaders proposed the plan in April 2021 to try to ease the violence that erupted after the army seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi

Southeast Asian leaders said on Sunday (November 15, 2026) that Myanmar has failed to comply with a 2021 peace plan and that its military and other armed groups continue to attack civilians, prompting them to extend a ban on Myanmar's leader attending the bloc's annual summits.

The stern rebuke by leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, who opened their annual summit meetings in the Philippine capital on Sunday (November 14, 2026), came during a review of the progress on the five-point peace plan by the country's military-backed government. Myanmar is a member of the 11-nation regional bloc.

ASEAN leaders proposed the plan in April 2021 to try to ease the violence that erupted after the army seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi. The army's takeover triggered widespread pro-democracy protests that were brutally quashed, leading to armed resistance and a civil war that has spread over much of the country.

The leaders reiterated “deep concern” over insufficient progress in implementing the peace plan. They urged all parties and stakeholders in Myanmar, "in particular the armed forces, security forces and armed groups to de-escalate violence and stop targeted attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure and enhance trust-building efforts.”

The three-day summit, which includes scheduled talks with world leaders led by U.S. President Donald Trump, will focus on conflicts, including the war in Myanmar, according to drafts of post-summit communiques seen by The Associated Press .

articles.title: Taliban authorities ban cricket on Kandahar radio
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The government has shown support for the game, hosting cricket matches during the August anniversary of its return to power

The Taliban authorities have banned radio stations in southern Kandahar from airing content related to cricket, a rapidly growing sport in Afghanistan, two broadcasters and a provincial source told AFP on Sunday (November 15, 2026).
The government has shown support for the game, hosting cricket matches during the August anniversary of its return to power.
But the provincial Information and Culture Department told radio stations on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that anything related to cricket is no longer allowed.
A source from that department, who requested anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the media, confirmed that “cricket coverage is banned”.
“Both commentary and news coverage, or even reporting about their winning result, is also banned,” he told AFP , without providing further details.
The head of a local radio station told AFP : “We received a call from Information and Culture, and we were told that we can’t cover cricket on the radio anymore.”
The manager of another Kandahar radio station confirmed the directive, saying that the authorities called and said “anything related to cricket is banned for now”.
Both broadcasters spoke to AFP on condition of anonymity for security reasons.
Afghanistan’s cricket board did not respond immediately to an AFP request for comment on the decision in Kandahar, which is home to the country’s supreme leader.
The Taliban authorities have restricted some sports in Afghanistan — outlawing mixed martial arts — but have allowed men and boys to continue playing cricket.

articles.title: Respiratory illnesses rise in Gaza with worst to come as winter floods arrive, WHO says
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher

​The World Health Organisation warned on Friday (November 13, 2026) of surging respiratory illnesses in Gaza, with worse expected after ‌heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians.

“The numbers ​already show the pressure. Acute respiratory infections are 33,000 cases higher than at ⁠the same time last year,” Dr. Reinhilde Van De Weerdt, WHO representative in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, told reporters in Geneva from Jerusalem.

Poor living conditions and severe overcrowding are driving up infections as Gaza’s population ‌is squeezed into an ever-smaller area, WHO said. The crunch has worsened as the Israeli military expands its control by advancing the “Yellow Line” — a demarcation established under ‌October’s U.S.-brokered ceasefire.
“That means people are living in more crowded conditions, where of course ‌the ⁠spread between humans of a virus is much more prone to spread,” Ms. Van ⁠De Weerdt explained.

The Israeli military told Reuters the Yellow Line aims to protect Israeli civilians and army troops from threats and that adjustments to its location follow the ceasefire agreement and international law, and are not intended ​to harm the civilian population.
“The IDF categorically ‌rejects the claim that it operates to deliberately reduce the area available to the civilian population in the Gaza Strip.”

COGAT, the Israeli military agency that coordinates aid, said that more than 93,000 tents and over 8,600 trucks carrying tarpaulin sheets, blankets and winter clothing ‌have entered Gaza since the Board of Peace, UN agencies and NGOs launched ​the winterisation plan. Equipment intended for the reconstruction of Gaza will be permitted to enter only after Hamas has been fully disarmed, it added.
Last week ⁠COGAT said that it had stepped up efforts to improve sanitary conditions before the heavy rain, in coordination with international organisations.
Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher.
“It is shocking that just a few days of rain really showed us what the coming months will bring. And winter has not even fully set in. The worst really is yet to come,” Ms. Van De Weerdt said.

Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher

​The World Health Organisation warned on Friday (November 13, 2026) of surging respiratory illnesses in Gaza, with worse expected after ‌heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians.

“The numbers ​already show the pressure. Acute respiratory infections are 33,000 cases higher than at ⁠the same time last year,” Dr. Reinhilde Van De Weerdt, WHO representative in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, told reporters in Geneva from Jerusalem.

Poor living conditions and severe overcrowding are driving up infections as Gaza’s population ‌is squeezed into an ever-smaller area, WHO said. The crunch has worsened as the Israeli military expands its control by advancing the “Yellow Line” — a demarcation established under ‌October’s U.S.-brokered ceasefire.

“That means people are living in more crowded conditions, where of course ‌the ⁠spread between humans of a virus is much more prone to spread,” Ms. Van ⁠De Weerdt explained.

The Israeli military told Reuters the Yellow Line aims to protect Israeli civilians and army troops from threats and that adjustments to its location follow the ceasefire agreement and international law, and are not intended ​to harm the civilian population.

“The IDF categorically ‌rejects the claim that it operates to deliberately reduce the area available to the civilian population in the Gaza Strip.”

COGAT, the Israeli military agency that coordinates aid, said that more than 93,000 tents and over 8,600 trucks carrying tarpaulin sheets, blankets and winter clothing ‌have entered Gaza since the Board of Peace, UN agencies and NGOs launched ​the winterisation plan. Equipment intended for the reconstruction of Gaza will be permitted to enter only after Hamas has been fully disarmed, it added.

Last week ⁠COGAT said that it had stepped up efforts to improve sanitary conditions before the heavy rain, in coordination with international organisations.

Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher.

“It is shocking that just a few days of rain really showed us what the coming months will bring. And winter has not even fully set in. The worst really is yet to come,” Ms. Van De Weerdt said.

articles.title: Drone ownership ban comes into force in Beijing over security concerns
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The ban applies to both urbanised and rural areas in the municipality of around 16,400 square kilometres (6,300 square miles) — an area roughly half the size of Belgium
Beijing’s ban on possessing drones came into force on Sunday (November 15, 2026), a measure authorities said will help ensure the security of China’s capital city.
The ban applies to both urbanised and rural areas in the municipality of around 16,400 square kilometres (6,300 square miles) — an area roughly half the size of Belgium.
The ban, which Beijing announced in September, outlaws owning and storing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to “safeguard the security of the capital”.
Transporting drones or their components into the city was also forbidden.
Owners had been forced to get rid of their devices ahead of Sunday’s (November 15, 2026) implementation, either by reselling them at approved buy-back points or online.
They could also have transported them outside the enforcement area.
Beijing, home to China’s central government, top leaders and the headquarters of the ruling Chinese Communist Party (CCP), has faced strict security measures.
The ban comes after airspace safety fears were raised in June when a small plane crashed into the city’s tallest skyscraper, killing the pilot and injuring 13 others.
Beijing had already banned drone sales in May 2026, with owners required to register their devices with authorities but permitted to keep them.
Now, anyone in possession of a drone could face a fine and the confiscation of their equipment.

articles.title: Yemeni government forces retreat from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February

Yemeni government forces announced on Sunday (November 15, 2026) that they were withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on a defence of their ​main base in Aden, in a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The announcement signalled the apparent ‌end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the ​Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that ⁠squeezed oil exports.

Sunday's announcement of a government retreat raises the prospect of new Houthi advances towards Aden, and underscores the predicament faced by Saudi Arabia in trying to stop the Houthis' drone and missile attacks on the kingdom. The government ‌forces have been based in Aden on the southern coast since 2015 after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.

Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February.

"The Southern Armed Forces announce the ⁠implementation of a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate," the main military force fighting for Yemen's government in the south of the country said in a statement.
"This step is taken based ​on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, ‌and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats."
There was no immediate response from the Houthis, or from Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government's main international ally.

Yemen's decade-long civil war, which had been dormant since 2022, abruptly reignited this summer as a ‌spillover from the Iran conflict. The Houthis made rapid gains to capture the coast along the ​Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which controls access to it, while besieging government forces in Taiz, the country's third-biggest city, in mountains above the approach to Aden.

A ⁠Saudi-backed government offensive last month rapidly retook key positions around the strait, notably Dhubab, but failed to drive the Houthis entirely away from the area or to retake the city of al-Mocha further up the coast.

The ‌Houthis have responded by intensifying drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, grounding flights with strikes on its main airports as well as setting global energy markets on edge by targeting energy facilities.

fullParagraphs: Mumbai will host the sixth annual Earthshot Prize Awards on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), with Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, attending the ceremony that will recognise five winners from among 15 finalists developing solutions to some of the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. Take That will perform their new song Higher ,alongside one of their popular hits, while Indian composer Shashwat Sachdev will close the show.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.
• In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

fullParagraphs: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

articles.title: Librarian P.V. Konnur felicitated on his 75th birth anniversary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Friends, colleagues and admirers of P.V. Konnur, the library science professional and president of LIS Academy, Bengaluru, felicitated him on his 75th birth anniversary.
The Amruta Mahotsava was held at the Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University on Thursday.

Ramesh B., Vice-Chancellor of Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University, released the felicitation volume brought out in Prof. Konnur’s honour and he said that such a dedicated librarian is very hard to find today, and that Prof. Konnur is a role model for budding librarians.

He observed that the librarian’s role has become more challenging, as students now have to be drawn back to libraries from their mobile phones. He urged Prof. Konnur to lead this movement and to help university libraries become experiential centres.
